goal: invoke_iteration_with_client exposes a mid-turn seam that surfaces ClaudeSDKClient.get_context_usage() readings to a harness-supplied observer each watcher poll and accepts a harness-initiated recovery interrupt that raises a signal distinguishable from operator-interrupt and external cancel.

references: src/flywheel/invoker_client.py:329 -- the _watcher() poll loop where get_context_usage() should be read once per poll_interval and the recovery-interrupt request checked; mirror the existing interrupt_flag/stop machinery (invoker_client.py:322-362)

src/flywheel/invoker_client.py:346 -- the operator-interrupt path flips interrupt_flag and cancels the iteration task routing through _handle_interrupt; the harness-recovery interrupt must be a DISTINCT channel that does NOT masquerade as operator-interrupt
src/flywheel/harness.py:2569 -- the _HangDetected-vs-external-CancelledError split is the precedent for making a harness-initiated cancel distinguishable from an outside cancel
constraints: All new parameters MUST be optional and default to None/no-op so every existing invoke_iteration_with_client caller (the plain harness call site) and the existing test suite are unchanged -- spec FR-2 off-by-default.

Read get_context_usage() at most once per poll_interval (not per message) and only when the live client exposes it; if the client lacks the method or it raises, surface nothing and continue (spec Error Handling: fall back silently to the AssistantMessage.usage estimate).

The harness-recovery interrupt must call ClaudeSDKClient.interrupt and then raise a signal the harness can tell apart from operator-interrupt (interrupt_flag path) and from an external SIGINT/SIGTERM CancelledError -- do NOT reuse the operator interrupt_flag for it.

Drive the watcher's client interactions through the existing client_factory test seam (tests/test_invoker_client.py) with a scripted fake client exposing get_context_usage and interrupt -- never open a real SDK/network session.
Commit with a Conventional Commits message (feat: ...) before emitting intent=verify.
non_goals: Do not compute occupancy ratios, capacity, thresholds, or recovery decisions here -- this task only plumbs the SDK reading out and the interrupt request in; the harness observe/act tasks own the policy.
Do not emit harness.context_threshold_crossed or harness.context_recovery events here.
Do not change the operator interrupt control-command path or add a new CONTROL_COMMAND_* verb.
edge_cases: Client without get_context_usage (plain query path or older client) -> observer simply receives no SDK reading; no error.
get_context_usage() raises mid-poll -> swallow, continue polling, no surfaced error.

Harness-recovery interrupt and a near-simultaneous normal completion -> honor whichever lands; the distinguishable signal is consulted only when the await actually raised (mirror harness.py:2575 race handling).
